stories.headline: HONNE Turns 10 and Neptune Theatre Gets the Party
stories.body: British duo HONNE brings their 10 Year Anniversary Tour to the Neptune Theatre tonight, Monday June 22 at 8pm — a milestone lap around the sun for the silky R&B-pop act that basically soundtracked every Seattle coffee-shop breakup of the 2010s. Support comes from Beka, so arrive early. The Neptune is an all-ages room with a bar for those holding valid ID.

stories.headline: Storm Host Dallas Wings in a Must-Watch Monday Matchup
stories.body: The Seattle Storm tip off against the Dallas Wings at Climate Pledge Arena tonight, June 22 at 7pm — prime summer WNBA action just steps from Seattle Center. Grab a bag of popcorn, pick a side of the court, and prepare to be genuinely loud about it.

stories.headline: ArtsWest's 'Wish You Were Here' Still Has Weeks to Go
stories.body: ArtsWest Playhouse is staging *Wish You Were Here*, a play exploring the political tension facing Iranian women, through July 5, 2026 — so you have plenty of time to catch what's shaping up to be a powerful West Seattle production. Performances run at 7312 West Green Lake Drive N; check the ArtsWest site for exact showtimes and the $25 industry discount.

stories.headline: Free Locks Concerts Are Back and Blankets Are Required
stories.body: Every weekend through September 7, the lawn at Hiram M. Chittenden Locks transforms into one of Seattle's best free concert venues — bring a picnic, chairs, and blankets (but leave the wine at home, no alcohol allowed). The series runs Saturdays and Sundays at 2pm; rain may cancel, so check ahead. It's the kind of afternoon that makes you remember why you live here.

stories.headline: Eight Bites, One Guide, Zero Regrets at Pike Place
stories.body: The Chef Guided Food Tour of Pike Place Market runs daily now through December 31, offering $75 tastings from eight artisan vendors with a friendly local guide. Meet at Simply Seattle at 1600 1st Ave — a 90-minute deep dive into the stalls most tourists sprint past. Perfect for a first-timer or a twenty-year local who somehow still hasn't tried that smoked salmon guy.
stories.location: Pike Place Market · Daily, through Dec 31

stories.headline: City Parks Become Cinemas Starting Wednesday Night
stories.body: Center City Cinema kicks off its summer run on Wednesday, June 24 and continues through August 28, turning Seattle parks into open-air movie theaters — bring blankets, chairs, and snacks for a very PNW night out. The series is free, but may be cancelled if it rains (so, you know, check the forecast and maybe bring an extra layer anyway). The full schedule of park locations is available on the Center City Cinema site.
